title: Localization of shifted derived Hom from a bounded-below compact source
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $R_t=R[1/t]$, the sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], and $F:D(R)\to D(R_t)$ for the functor induced termwise by exact scalar localization $M\mapsto R_t\otimes_R M$, with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the exact-functor derived construction [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Fix $K\in D(R)$ with the following property: for every countable family $(L_n)$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L_n[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,(\bigoplus_nL_n)[q])$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below $L\in D(R)$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the actual scalar-extension map induces an isomorphism of $A[1/t]$-modules
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])[1/t]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_t)}(FK,FL[q]),\qquad u/t^n\longmapsto t^{-n}F(u).$$
Localization of the Hom module has the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. These isomorphisms are natural in $K,L$, commute with shifts, and respect identity maps and composition whenever the displayed hypotheses hold for the objects involved. No constructibility, scheme, or essential-surjectivity assertion is included.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:R\to R_t$ be the localization map and $U=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. First, $M\mapsto R_t\otimes_RM$ is exact on module sheaves. Let $L_t$ be the presheaf $V\mapsto R(V)[1/t]$, so $R_t=L_t^\#$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] (with $\mathcal O=R$, $\mathcal G=M$, $\mathcal F=L_t$) there is an isomorphism $M\otimes_RR_t\cong(M\otimes_{p,R}L_t)^\#$, natural in $M$, with $(M\otimes_{p,R}L_t)(V)=M(V)\otimes_{R(V)}R(V)[1/t]$. If $M'\to M$ is a monomorphism of sheaves, then each $M'(V)\to M(V)$ is injective, because kernels are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The maps $M'(V)\otimes R(V)[1/t]\to M(V)\otimes R(V)[1/t]$ stay injective because $R(V)\to R(V)[1/t]$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and sheafification preserves monomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]. The functor $-\otimes_RR_t$ preserves cokernels as a left adjoint [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], so it is exact on $R$-modules. Since $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ does not change the underlying abelian sheaves, it is also exact as a functor to $R_t$-modules. Hence the termwise functor induces $F:D(R)\to D(R_t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], and $U$ is induced termwise. By that node, $F$ with $FQ\cong Q(-\otimes_RR_t)$ is a left derived functor (a right Kan extension along $Q$) of the termwise change of rings. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2), $L\varphi^*$ is the left derived functor of the same termwise functor, computed on K-flat complexes. Uniqueness of Kan extensions gives a unique isomorphism $L\varphi^*\cong F$ compatible with the maps from $Q(-\otimes_RR_t)$. On a K-flat representative $P$ it is the identity of $Q(P\otimes_RR_t)$ under $c_P$. Transport the adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] along this isomorphism. This gives bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_t)}(FK,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,UM)$$ natural in $K\in D(R)$ and $M\in D(R_t)$. By its clause (1), and by naturality of the unit for an arbitrary complex replaced by a K-flat resolution, the unit $\eta_L:L\to UFL$ is the class of the termwise map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Both $F$ and $U$ commute strictly with the shift on complexes, and the bijections are compatible with these identifications.

proof.text: For bounded-below $L$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-underlying-telescope]. It identifies $UFL$ with the telescope triangle of the sequence $L\xrightarrow{t}L\xrightarrow{t}\cdots$, and identifies the stage-$n$ leg with the scalar-extension unit followed by multiplication by $t^{-n}$. After shifting by $q$, the same identification holds for $UFL[q]$.

Fix $q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sequence-relative-hom-telescope] in $D(R)$ to $K$, the sequence $X_n=L[q]$ with transition $t$, and the telescope vertex $UFL[q]$. Its two coproduct comparison hypotheses are exactly the hypothesis on $K$ in the statement, applied to the constant countable families $L[q]$ and $L[q+1]$; both have a common lower bound because $L$ is bounded below. We obtain
$$\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,UFL[q]).$$
The stage map sends $u:K\to L[q]$ to the composite with the $n$th telescope leg.

source.place: Tags 093W, 0CRK and 094A; the sequence-relative Hom telescope lemma

proof.text:
Compose the bijection of Step 3 with the adjunction of Step 1 for $M=FL[q]$, using the identification of $UFL[q]$ with the telescope vertex from Step 2. This gives a natural isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_t)}(FK,FL[q]).$$
At stage $n$ a map $u$ goes to the adjunct of $(t^{-n}\circ\eta_L)[q]\circ u$, by the leg normalization of Step 2, where $\eta_L$ is the unit identified in Step 1. For any adjunction the adjunct of $U(g)\circ\eta\circ u$ is $g\circ F(u)$. Here $t^{-n}$ on $UFL$ is $U$ of the automorphism $t^{-n}$ of $FL$: $t$ is a unit of $R_t$, so it acts invertibly on $FL$. Hence the image is $t^{-n}F(u)$.

The colimit in Step 4 has transition $u\mapsto t u$. By the fraction relation in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], it is canonically $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])[1/t]$, with the class at stage $n$ written $u/t^n$. Under this identification the preceding map is $u/t^n\mapsto t^{-n}F(u)$, proving the displayed isomorphism. Naturality in $K,L$, compatibility with shifts, and preservation of identities and composition follow from naturality of the adjunction and of the telescope legs, together with bilinearity of composition and the fraction relation.
